title: Automated KV quant calibration sweep and latency/quality SLO analysis for INT8/FP8
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated calibration and evaluation pipeline to characterize INT8 and FP8 KV cache quant profiles across representative production prompt distributions and quantify latency/quality trade-offs. This ticket implements an autosweep harness that (1) generates per-layer scale candidates using layer-wise activations from a mixed traffic sample, (2) runs offline accuracy regressions (perplexity, token-level edit distance, and targeted QA accuracy) on benchmark prompt-sets, and (3) runs throughput/latency microbenchmarks across batch sizes and sequence lengths. Acceptance criteria: 1) a reproducible calibration pipeline that outputs canonical profile artifacts, 2) an eval dashboard with regression alerts and thresholded SLO checks (p50/p95/p99 latency and QA delta), and 3) a recommendation matrix (INT8/FP8/mixed) with deployment-rules for hot vs cold KV regions.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff - scoped calibration dataset. We sampled 1.2M tokens across webhooks, chat history, and code completions to get a realistic prefix distribution (heavy tail on short prefixes, 15% long-context >1024). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Quant+Calibration

2026-02-26: Prototype autotune script finished (calib-v1). It extracts per-layer max/mean of KV activations, fits a per-head asymmetric scale, and writes candidate profiles. Ran quick sanity checks vs fp16 baseline on redwood-llama3-13B-qa. Results looked promising for memory but accuracy regressions visible on long-context QA prompts.

2026-03-02: First sweep results uploaded to dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-quant-sweep-27103. Summary: INT8 reduced KV memory by ~3.3x and average token cost ~26% on our serving traces. Median latency delta small (+1-3ms), but p99 increased by ~18% on 40-token responses on A100 80GB due to dequantize overhead and non-coalesced reads in some layers.

2026-03-04: Accuracy validation - two failure modes identified: (a) drift in attention distribution for long prefixes where per-layer single-scale INT8 under-represents rare large activations, (b) head-wise skew producing localized hallucination on targeted QA prompts. We added per-head clipping and fallback to FP8 for the top 3 heads in each layer as an experimental mitigation.

2026-03-06: Performance optimization - changed memory layout for quantized KV to coalesce dequantize ops and prefetch scales. Measured p99 improvement ~9% over previous sweep. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892

2026-03-08: Review feedback from ML infra (Lars Müller): suggested adding a synthetic adversarial prefix set (edge-case long-retention) and measure prefix-replay cache hit behavior with quantized profiles. Action: add synthetic set and extend harness to replay exact cache sequences to reproduce drift.

2026-03-09: Decision: adopt an adaptive profile strategy: use INT8 for cold KV segments (prefix length < 512 and low activation variance), FP8 for hot/high-variance KV segments, and allow per-head FP fallback for layers that exceed regression thresholds. This gives a balanced cost/latency/quality trade-off for most customers.

2026-03-10: Next steps: (1) integrate calibration pipeline into CI to produce canonical artifacts for each model build, (2) add automated regression gating that fails PRs when QA accuracy delta > 1.5% or p99 latency increase > 10% vs baseline, (3) document deployment rules for Dedicated customers (config knobs and rollout safety checks).

Artifacts: Confluence design doc, autotune script in runtime repo under /tools/kv_quant, PR #4892, eval dashboard. Recommended follow-ups: short A/B test in Dedicated with 5% traffic, and a canary for Private customers with strict p99 alerts.
